items.title: ‘Genuine’ vs ‘political’: The social media campaign pitting Ranchi protests against CJP
items.summary: As Jharkhand’s student protest against alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) builds momentum in Ranchi, sections on social media have tried to cast it as the ‘genuine’ counterpart to the Cockroach Janta Party-led protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, the one ‘without foreign funding’ and ‘led by students’. Even when protesters on the ground, and the evidence itself, tell a different story of shared solidarity and mutual inspiration, not rivalry. Using specific keywords, Newslaundry conducted searches across Facebook and X to track online discussions around the two protests. This analysis identified recurring narratives praising the Jharkhand protest while contrasting it with CJP's month-long protest against the NEET-UG exam paper leak in Delhi that ended with Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation on July 25. The CJP protest faced allegations of foreign funding, political backing, ‘Azadi’ slogans and violence. Same accounts, different angle At least two posts followed identical templates and were traced back to accounts that had separately criticised CJP. One Facebook post read: “Student power is a wave of the people – no hooliganism, no shouting, no inflammatory statements, no stone-throwing, no anti-national talk. No abuse. Just students peacefully protesting for their rights, focused on student interests.” The post went on to allege that Jharkhand Police had “brutally lathi-charged” students and questioned why political leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and Arvind Kejriwal, had remained silent. As Andhra Pradesh’s fare-free bus travel scheme for women, Stree Shakti, completed one year on August 15, officials said that on average, women avail 24 lakh bus rides under the scheme daily. Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu travelled in an RTC bus on August 15 from the Parade Ground to Camp Office in the Amaravati region and interacted with a few women passengers. A total of 87 crore fare-free bus rides have been completed in one year of the scheme being in effect, Naidu said, making the daily average around 24 lakh rides. The Stree Shakti scheme is currently being implemented in 7,631 Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) buses, covering about 76% of the corporation’s fleet, according to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office. The government is subsidising bus fares worth around Rs 8.53 crore a day, amounting to a total of Rs 3,095 crore so far, the statement said. It also noted that after the scheme was introduced, women’s occupancy in RTC buses increased to 62%. Naidu stated that through the Stree Shakti scheme, women are getting to save money, and use those savings for family and livelihood needs. He said that the scheme has enhanced women's freedom of movement, financial independence, and self-confidence. The CM spoke to students and working women, including a fisherwoman and a weaver, about how the scheme has impacted them. The women reportedly told the CM that the scheme has made it easier to access education, source materials for work, and sell produce in markets.

Activists monitoring the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Telangana have urged the Election Commission to give a chance to challenge any wrongful categorisations under the Absent, Shifted, Duplicate, Dead and Others (ASDDO) or ‘uncollectable’ tag. Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C Sudarshan Reddy had recently announced that by the end of the enumeration period which concluded on August 10, around 73.39 lakh enumeration forms, or 21.70% of the total voters in the state, were classified as “uncollectable”. Of these, 9.22 lakh voters were marked as dead, 11.25 lakh were classified as absent or untraceable, 45.18 lakh voters were found to have permanently shifted, while 6.70 lakh were marked as already enrolled. Around 1.02 lakh voters were listed under the ‘others’ category. While the draft electoral roll is set to be published on August 17, activists SQ Masood and MA Mujeeb argued that such a large number of electors need additional safeguards before being potentially deleted. They sought 15 days of additional time to provide an effective opportunity to challenge any wrongful ASDDO/uncollectable categorisation before publication of the draft electoral roll. In a press release issued on August 15, Masood and Mujeeb, who run the civil society organisations ASEEM and ADALAH, stressed that not collecting or submitting an enumeration form alone cannot establish that an elector is dead, permanently shifted or otherwise ineligible to remain enrolled. They sought a minimum 15-day extension before publishing the draft roll, to provide voters categorised as ASDD/uncollectable a chance to verify their ASDD status and challenge any incorrect categorisation. They also urged the ECI to protect the continuity of existing voters’ registration and electoral record, noting that an elector who has been enrolled for many years could potentially find their name wrongfully omitted from the draft roll and subsequently be required to submit a fresh Form-6 application, which is used by a person to seek inclusion of their name in the electoral roll as a new voter. “An error during enumeration should not erase an elector's electoral history. A speech by a Kerala University Vice-Chancellor at a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) event has sparked a political controversy in the state after he said that those who oppose singing Vande Mataram do not know who their mother is. Mohanan Kunnummal, Vice-Chancellor of the Kerala University of Health Sciences (KUHS) and acting Vice-Chancellor of the University of Kerala, made the remarks while delivering the Independence Day message at Sankalp 2026, an RSS-organised gathering of youth, in Neyyattinkara, Thiruvananthapuram, on Saturday, August 15. In his speech, Mohanan Kunnummal said that the mother holds an important place in Indian culture, which is why India is referred to as Bharatamba (Mother India) and why Vande Mataram is sung. He added that those who oppose saying Vande Mataram are people who do not know their mother. “In India, the mother is of paramount importance; hence, we refer to India as ‘Bharat Mata’ (Mother India). That is why we pray by saying Vande Mataram. Those who oppose saying Vande Mataram are people who don’t know who the mother is. Those who know who the mother is and understand what a mother means will always say Vande Mataram,” he said. Mohanan Kunnummal later told The Hindu that his reference to “mother” was part of a longer speech and referred to the motherland. The Student Federation of India (SFI), the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)], and the All India Students' Federation (AISF) criticised the Vice-Chancellor's remarks. items.title: CAG report says not even half of emergency disaster funds transferred to states
items.summary: The Union government has not spent even half of the funds under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), meant for meeting expenses for emergency response related to disasters. More than 53% of funds, which would supplement the State Disaster Response Funds, remains unutilised, as per a report of Comptroller and Auditor General of India based on the accounts of Union government in 2024-25, tabled at the Parliament the other day. Of the total Rs 11,474 crore sanctioned under NDRF as assistance to the state for calamities of severe nature, only Rs 5356 crore was transferred to the states. The remaining Rs 6117.97 crore is listed as ‘savings’ in the CAG report to indicate that it was unspent. This comes at a time when several states, including Kerala and Assam, are alleging that the Union government ignored its demand for more NRDF funds during devastating natural calamities. CAG has noted this glaring disparity in the head ‘Transfers to state’, which also include assistance to state from National Disaster Mitigation Funds (NDMF) and special assistance. Nearly 75 % of funds under NDMF and over 83 % of special assistance to states were not transferred. The sanction provision for special assistance was Rs 20,000 crore, of which only Rs 3350 was spent. Under NDMF to states, only 719.72 crore was transferred from the sanctioned amount of Rs 2868 crore. In addition to these, the Union government has a grant worth Rs 100 crore which can be transferred to states as ‘Loans as advance assistance for relief on account of natural calamities’. The government has not utilised a single penny from this account. While NDRF is used towards meeting the expenses for emergency response, relief and rehabilitation, the NDMF is for implementing schemes aimed at reducing the risk or impact of a disaster. The CAG has noted that there has been persistent savings under ‘Transfers to states’ under various schemes in the financial years, 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. The under utilised amounts of these periods were respectively Rs 67,882 crore, Rs 46,012.89 crore and Rs 36,219 crore. “Persistent savings were registered despite being regularly pointed out in our Audit Reports and the advisory issued by MoF (Ministry of Finance) on realistic budgeting on the directions of the Public Accounts Committee,” the CAG report said. items.summary: The Kerala High Court has questioned the conduct of the police in the investigation into the death of Nithin Raj, a student of Anjarakandy Dental College, stating that the sequence of events raises suspicion that senior officials tried to protect the prime accused, Dr MK Ram. Justice A Badharudeen, on July 22, Wednesday, while hearing a petition filed by Nithin's parents, observed that the manner in which Ram, a former faculty member of the college, was arrested appeared to have paved the way for his release on bail. The court said the mandatory safeguards laid down by the Supreme Court during arrest did not appear to have been followed, raising serious doubts about the police's handling of the case. The court ordered a thorough inquiry into the circumstances that led to Ram securing bail from the Thalassery Special Court dealing with cases under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. It cautioned that if the police failed to conduct a credible probe, the High Court would consider initiating its own inquiry, which could include scrutiny of the phone records of those allegedly involved. Justice Badharudeen directed the Investigating Officer to appear before the court on Friday with the complete records placed before the Sessions Court at the time of remand. The officer has also been asked to submit a sworn statement explaining whether the Supreme Court's directions on informing an accused of the reasons for arrest were complied with. The High Court further sought a copy of the bail order and called for a report from the Special Court on whether it had verified compliance with the apex court's arrest guidelines before granting bail. The court also cast doubt on the investigation's earlier conclusion that Nithin's death was linked to harassment over app-based loans, indicating that the available materials required closer examination. It further remarked that the decision to replace the original investigation team immediately after criticism from the court gave the impression that attention was being diverted from alleged lapses in the probe.
